text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

The origin of idle rumours known as "furphies" can be traced to JOHN FURPHY an Australian blacksmith and engineer who was born in 1842. His iron water tanks were mounted on wheels and used during World War I. The "furphies" were said to have been spread by the drivers.
West Australian academic, essayist and pioneer broadcaster SIR WALTER MURDOCH was born in 1874.
The British aviation pioneer SIR FRANCIS CHICHESTER, who was the first to sail solo round the world in 1966/67, was born in 1901.

American country singer HANK WILLIAMS (HIRAM KING) was born in 1923. His first records were cut in 1946. He appeared in the pop charts for the first time with "Move It On Over" (1947). Further hits included "Love Sick Blues" (1949), "Cold Cold Heart" (1951), "Hey Good Lookin" (1951) and "Your Cheatin' Heart" (1953). Most of his songs were million sellers. Despite his success he had personal problems and died at the age of 29 in 1953. His death was blamed on his excessive drinking. In 1961 he was entered in the Country Music Hall of Fame and in 1987 in the Rock 'n' Roll Hall Of Fame.
American actress ANNE BANCROFT was born in 1931. She won an Oscar for her role in "The Miracle Worker". Other films included "The Graduate".

US singer and songwriter with 'The Tubes', FEE WAYBILL, was born in 1950. The group formed at the end of the 1960s. FEE only became a member because he was the only one who had a car large enough to accommodate all their instruments. It was not until later that it turned out he could sing. From 1976 they began to chart and their biggest hit was "She's A Beauty" (1983).
** EVENTS **
1792 : The Crown Jewels were stolen in Paris.
1892 : The gold rush in Western Australia was started by
two men reporting a find at Coolgardie. A.W.BAYLEY and W.FORD brought nearly 160 kg of gold into the Southern Cross bank.
1893 : The first licence number plates for cars were
introduced in France.
1910 : London doctors reported that if lunacy increased
at the current rate the insane would outnumber the sane by 1950. 1931 : Long-playing records were demonstrated in New York by
RCA-Victor.
1945 : The release of Australian POWs by Japan revealed

terrible stories of torture, starvation and death in many camps in Burma, Thailand, Singapore, Malaya, Java, Borneo and the Pacific Islands. In June 1947 The War Crimes commission sentenced Japanese officer MASAO BABA to death for atrocities against allied prisoners of war.
1961 : A huge "ban the bomb" demonstration in London

ended with 830 arrests after police tried to move thousands of protestors staging a sit-down protest. Among those arrested were actress VANESSA REDGRAVE, playwright JOHN OSBORNE and the chairman of the campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, CANON COLLINS. 1969 : Australian-made television crime shows "Homocide" and
"Division 4" were criticised by the Broadcasting Control Board for excessive violence.
1974 : Australian radio and television licences were
abolished.
1977 : Prima donna MARIA CALLAS died of a heart attack in
her Paris flat. The Greek opera singer was 53.
1980 : The movie "Breaker Morant" scooped the pool with
eight wins at the Australian Film Awards.
1985 : The woman whose romantic styles and fabrics

dressed a generation and still decorate homes died of a fall. Welsh-born LAURA ASHLEY was 60. She began designing tea-towels on her kitchen table. At the time of her death she was deputy chairman of a large international business employing four thousand people. She branched into flowery clothes and then into furnishings with a country flavour.
1985 : Jelly babies were withdrawn from sale in West
Germany. Traces of an illegal sweetner, based on anti-freeze, were discovered in the lollies.
1991 : The first direct elections were held in Hong Kong.
Seventeen of the 18 seats went to candidates who were strongly opposed to both the Hong Kong and Chinese governments. China is due to take back control of Hong Kong in 1997.
